text:
incident-bot: INC: continuous-batching latency spike detected (p90 -> 5s) for /v1/generate under high concurrency. Auto-alert fired.
elaine: seeing customer reports from two enterprise tenants timing out. digging into traces now.
samir: I can take it — currently looking at batcher metrics, queue depth is climbing fast.
sophia: can you confirm if kv-cache hit rate changed? might be cascade from cache eviction.
samir: kv-cache hit rate actually stable. the obvious thing is microbatch growth: average microbatch size jumped from 8 -> 40 at high concurrency bursts.
elaine: that would explain per-request queueing. any backpressure?
samir: queue_capacity is set to 2000 requests; with sustained concurrency we get head-of-line blocking and microbatches keep growing until latency cliffs.
devon: timer jitter we added last week to reduce synchronized flushes — maybe it regressed under >400 rps.
elaine: okay plan: apply hotfix to cap microbatch size and re-enable per-worker jitter. can we hotpatch the batcher config without deploy?
sophia: yes, we have runtime config for the batcher. runtime: {"max_microbatch_size": 16, "jitter_ms": 30, "queue_capacity": 1000}. I'll push the config now.
samir: rolling to 4 zones, applying to hot path first. doing canary on zone-3 with 10% of traffic.
deploy-bot: config change applied to zone-3 canary (config-id: cb-hotfix-20260315-1).
elaine: monitor p50/p90 and microbatch size distribution. samir, can you throttle any backlogged workers if needed?
samir: can throttle. initial canary shows microbatch size dropping back to ~12 and p90 gone from 5s -> 350ms.
rajeev: good. what about customers already timed out? need communication.
elaine: ops: collect request IDs for failed requests and cross-check with logs; outreach to two tenants with RCA in progress.
sophia: also noticed some KV-cache thrash on a few hosts due to memory pressure from larger microbatches — proactively cleared small shard caches on those hosts.
devon: we should also add immediate mitigation in runtime: refuse new batched requests if queue depth > 75% to provide backpressure. can be a follow-up change.
samir: agree. I'll file a follow-up PR: "batcher: soft-drop above high-water mark + metrics" and link to thread.
elaine: handoff: i'm on for 30 more mins then handing to rajeev. rajeev, please watch SLOs and customer tickets. escalate if anything re-spikes.
rajeev: taking handoff. setting alert on microbatch median > 20 and queue_depth > 1500.
sophia: note for postmortem: correlate microbatch growth to recently-deployed scheduling tweak from 2026-03-14 (jitter reduction). get diffs.
elaine: tentative owner for postmortem: samir + sophia. include timeline, config diffs, customer impact, and follow-ups: backpressure, canary ramp limits, additional observability.
samir: PR for follow-up backpressure created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/batcher/pulls/487.
elaine: thanks team. I'll draft customer-facing note and tag support. leaving the channel — rajeev oncall. :white_check_mark:
rajeev: ack — i'll keep an eye and post updates.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: latency returned to baseline after config hotfix. Marking as "mitigated".
elaine: leaving a short runbook entry in ops-runbooks/batcher-mitigation.md with steps: apply runtime config, canary 10%, monitor microbatch metrics, rollback link.
sophia: adding follow-up actions: re-run distributed jitter tuning under synthetic high-concurrency load, add unit test for max_microbatch_size enforcement, and schedule load run next week.
samir: postmortem owners assigned, will sync with product for customer comms.
devon: reminder: add synthetic alert that fires when microbatch variance spikes — caught this early today.
rajeev: closing notes: no data exfil, limited 2 tenants saw timeouts for ~7 minutes peak, mitigated by hotfix. will update incident tracking ticket.
incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20260315-0892 (severity: P2).
